messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "problem_statement": "Duplicate claims submitted through different channels are not being identified by the system.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "date": "2026-10-26T09:40:00Z",
   "quote": "It’s messy when the same claim twice comes in — one by phone, one online, and the system doesn’t flag it.",
   "route": "sales"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-09-04T08:05:00Z",
   "quote": "Claims: click \"Link to existing claim\", dead x1 ... Claims: click \"Next\"",
   "route": "sessions"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-09-18T09:38:00Z",
   "quote": "Claims: click \"Link to existing claim\", dead x1",
   "route": "sessions"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-25T16:14:00+00:00",
   "quote": "We’re seeing cases where the same claim twice appears because the system doesn’t alert staff when a matching incident already exists in intake — we’ve had to manually link them after the fact, which delays payments and reporting.",
   "route": "support"
  }
 ],
 "title": "Duplicate claims submitted through different channels are not being identified by the"
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The claim is that duplicate claims from different channels aren't flagged by the system, forcing manual linking and delaying payments. The support quote (2026-10-25) directly describes this product gap and its business impact, and the sales quote corroborates it. Session logs show users repeatedly clicking a 'Link to existing claim' button that appears dead, and the described manual workaround is itself signal per the rules. Nothing indicates an external cause, a help-article answer, or praise.", "verdict": "pass"}
